blogs.title: Two Diagnoses, One Presentation: Recognizing Concurrent Behçet’s and Neuro‑Behçet’s at the Front Door
blogs.description: Why BD and neuro‑BD rarely debut together, and how to spot it when they do. We’ll walk through high‑yield bedside clues (genital aphthae specificity, folliculitis‑like lesions, systemic inflammation) and apply the International Criteria for Behçet’s Disease to a febrile headache presentation. Practical tips for ED and admitting teams on when to pivot from infection‑first thinking to an inflammatory CNS frame.

blogs.title: Normal MRI, Abnormal Patient: Diagnosing Acute Neuro‑Behçet’s When Imaging Is Silent
blogs.description: Acute neuro‑BD can present as aseptic meningitis without parenchymal lesions; early MRI may be normal. This post reviews the CSF profile that supports the diagnosis, timing and utility of repeat imaging, red flags for alternative diagnoses, and how to avoid anchoring on a negative MRI in inflammatory CNS disease.

blogs.title: Hyponatremia With Hiccups: SIADH as a Neuro‑Inflammatory Signal in Behçet’s
blogs.description: Linking SIADH to acute neuro‑BD: proposed IL‑6–mediated mechanisms, distinguishing SIADH from other hyponatremia etiologies, and bedside clues like persistent hiccups and rhabdomyolysis. We’ll cover a pragmatic correction strategy (fluid restriction, monitoring, when to escalate) and pitfalls of over‑rapid sodium correction in inflammatory CNS settings.

blogs.title: Targeted Testing, Not Shotgunning: Diagnostic Stewardship in Febrile Neuro‑Inflammation
blogs.description: A case‑based critique of indiscriminate labs (ACE, sIL‑2R, broad autoantibodies, HLA‑B51) when clinical features don’t support them. We contrast their limited diagnostic yield with high‑value steps: infectious rule‑outs (HSV/VZV PCR, TB studies), CSF analysis, and careful serial exams. Frameworks for starting—and de‑escalating—empiric antimicrobials while pursuing an inflammatory CNS diagnosis.

blogs.title: Colchicine Alone in Acute Neuro‑Behçet’s: Fluke or Future?
blogs.description: Corticosteroids are standard for acute neuro‑BD, yet this case improved with colchicine monotherapy. We review existing evidence for colchicine in neuro‑BD, mechanistic plausibility (neutrophil modulation, IL‑1β/IL‑6 effects), when a steroid‑sparing trial might be reasonable, safety/monitoring (renal, hepatic, myotoxicity), and how to identify patients who still warrant early steroids or additional immunosuppression.

blogs.title: Oral and Genital Ulcers in the Febrile Patient With Headache: Building the Right Differential
blogs.description: A structured approach to oral/genital ulcers plus constitutional and neuro symptoms. We compare BD to mimics (HSV, syphilis, HIV seroconversion, reactive arthritis, IBD‑associated aphthae, Sweet’s, SLE, drug eruptions, malignancy), highlight distinguishing skin and ocular findings, and outline when to involve rheumatology, dermatology, and ophthalmology early.
